title: Set a miter saw to 45 degrees: squeeze its detent release, swing the arm into the stop, press the lock lever down
instruction: Set the miter saw to 45 degrees and lock it.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031.00, 889,700 US jobs in 2025, BLS) have as a core task "Shape or cut materials to specified measurements, using hand tools, machines, or power saws", and NCCER's carpentry module 27210-07 (trim) lists "Make square and miter cuts using a miter box or power miter saw." Setting the saw's table to 45 degrees is how the corners of casing, baseboard and frames are cut. The robot uses the saw's own controls as its manual says (SKIL MS6316-00, p. 25): hold the miter-lock lever and the detent release lever together, lift the release lever, rotate the arm, let the detent pin snap fully into the notch, then press the lock lever down until it clicks. What is hard: one hand squeezes two levers 4 cm apart, 5 cm above the bench, and keeps them squeezed while it drags the arm round a 45 degree arc past three other stops, lets the pin drop into the right one, and presses the lock home without disturbing the angle.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z above the table top (bases at y +305 and -305). (1) Plywood mounting board, 350 (x) x 420 (y) x 19, not clamped, front edge at x 460, centred on y 0, its four corners marked with tape. (2) SKIL MS6316-00 7-1/4 in sliding compound miter saw, 11.1 kg, bolted to the board through its four feet, front toward the robot, table pivot at x 600, y 0; unplugged, cord coiled behind it, dust bag and work clamp off, blade taken off, lower guard on and closed, head raised and slid back. Sizes read off the maker's drawings and photos, +-5: table surface 88 above the bench (69 above the board), turntable 170 across, fence 60 high, miter arm 56 wide reaching 265 from the pivot. Lock lever (black plastic, 30 wide, 22 thick, 84 long): hinged at the top of the arm's front end, up and level, its top 86 above the bench, its end 346 from the pivot; in the simulation it clicks 35 degrees down, which is not taken from the real saw. Detent release lever (black plastic, pad 16 x 22): under the arm's front end, pad 280 to 296 from the pivot, underside 45 above the bench. Starting state: 0 degrees, detent pin in the 0 notch, lock lever up. Stops at 0, 15, 22.5, 31.6 and 45 degrees each side; range 47 left to 50 right. A red pointer left of the arm reads a white scale on the base. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open, a layer of tape on the pads. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Only the end state counts, read with the saw's own pointer and scale, a ruler, a photo and the trial video; limits are inclusive. 1.0 = pointer within 0.5 degrees of 45 (left or right), release lever let go (within 1.5 degrees of its rest), lock lever pressed past its click and staying down (in the simulation 30 degrees or more below level), every fingertip 30 mm or more from the box round each part of the saw (so near a corner of the round guard's box a fingertip up to 46 mm from the guard reads as touching; the board does not count), and nothing moved for a full 0.5 s (arm 0.2 degrees, levers 1 degree, board corners 1 mm: each corner's largest spread in x, y and z, combined, so a 0.9 mm wander can read as 1.19 mm; sampled 20 times a second, so a jerk and return between samples is not seen); success: held for 1 s. 0.75 = pointer within 0.5 degrees of 45 and release lever let go, but not locked, or a fingertip closer than 30 mm, or something still moving. 0.5 = pointer within 0.5 degrees of 15, 22.5 or 31.6 (either side), release lever let go, locked or not. 0.25 = any other angle of 10 degrees or more, including 45 with the release lever still squeezed. 0 = under 10 degrees, whatever the levers; and 0 whenever any of the board's four marked corners is more than 10 mm from where it started, in any direction (slid, turned, tipped or lifted). The order of the steps is not scored: with the lock lever down the arm cannot be swung.
run_limit: 1,850 steps (92.5 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo needs about 740
reset_notes: Lift the lock lever until level, squeeze the release lever, swing the arm back to 0 and let go; check that the pointer reads 0 and the arm does not turn when pushed. Put the board back with its four corners on the tape marks on the table. Check the saw is unplugged and the blade is off. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at true size (+-5 mm). Forces NOT measured; estimates from a catalogue spring of the size in the maker's photo and friction arithmetic (README): release lever 13 N to start, 22 N with the pin out, 27 N at its stop; arm 13 N sideways at the levers; lock lever about 2.5 N m (30 N at its end). Pin, notches and clamp are rules in the code: squeezed 5.7 mm the pin is out; let go, the arm stays loose until moved less than 1 degree from a notch. Head fixed, raised; no blade.
